info.title: ConvoMem Integration API
info.description: Integration API for external AI agents (voice/chat): capture messages, resolve customers, manage conversations, and ingest/lookup memories.

apiKey.name: X-API-Key
apiKey.description: Organization API key from your dashboard. Prefix: sk-org-...

RetrievalLimit.name: limit
RetrievalLimit.description: Maximum memories returned; values above the server cap are clamped.

RetrievalThreshold.name: threshold
RetrievalThreshold.description: Fixed minimum retrieval score. Omit to use adaptive thresholding.

RetrievalRerank.name: rerank
RetrievalRerank.description: Opt into cross-encoder reranking for a smaller, higher-precision result set.

RetrievalLatestOnly.name: latestOnly
RetrievalLatestOnly.description: Collapse superseded lifecycle versions to the latest applicable memory.

RetrievalReferenceDate.name: referenceDate
RetrievalReferenceDate.description: Deterministic ISO 8601 evaluation time for temporal ranking and expiry.

RetrievalIncludeAgentFacts.name: includeAgentFacts
RetrievalIncludeAgentFacts.description: Include agent-authored commitments and disclosures; excluded by default.

RetrievalVerify.name: verify
RetrievalVerify.description: Override answerability verification for this lookup; may add a paid model call.

context.description: Formatted context string ready for LLM injection

tokenCount.description: Estimated token count of the context

retrievalConfig.description: Effective retrieval controls after server defaults and clamping.

post.summary: Capture a message and auto-manage session
post.description: Single endpoint for external integrators. Resolves customer identity, finds or creates an active conversation session, enqueues the message for memory extraction, and returns the session context. No explicit start/end lifecycle calls required. Accepts either a single message string or a full messages array (with user + assistant turns) — one is required.

schema.description: Either `message` or `messages` is required. At least one identity field (`customerId`, `externalId`, `email`, or `phoneNumber`) is required.

message.description: Single user message (simple form). Required if messages not provided.

messages.description: Full conversation turns including assistant replies. Required if message not provided.

language.description: Optional BCP-47 source-language hint for this turn

customerId.description: Identity field — at least one of customerId, externalId, email, or phoneNumber is required.

externalId.description: Identity field — at least one of customerId, externalId, email, or phoneNumber is required.

email.description: Identity field — at least one of customerId, externalId, email, or phoneNumber is required.

phoneNumber.description: Identity field — at least one of customerId, externalId, email, or phoneNumber is required.

userName.description: Customer display name — used to set or update the customer profile name (backfills placeholder names like phone numbers)

language.description: BCP-47 fallback for turns without their own language hint

occurredAt.description: Optional timestamp for a historical conversation. Omit for live captures. Extracted memories retain this source time for temporal retrieval and supersession.

infer.description: Set false to persist each non-system message directly as a memory without LLM extraction or entity inference. Content is still sanitized, sensitivity-filtered, embedded, deduplicated, reconciled, and speaker-scoped.

socialHandles.description: Identity field — social handles, either as bare strings ("@jane") or as objects with an optional platform. Counts toward the "at least one identity field" requirement.

endConversation.description: Close the conversation as COMPLETED once these turns are persisted. Use this instead of a separate call to POST /customers/conversations/end when you already know the call is over: capture writes the transcript in a background job, so closing separately races analysis against the write and can summarise half a call. Mutually exclusive with `escalate`.

outcome.description: Optional outcome recorded when `endConversation` is true.

escalate.description: Close the conversation as ESCALATED once these turns are persisted. Mutually exclusive with `endConversation`.

reason.description: Optional reason recorded when `escalate` is true.

speakerId.description:
Your own identifier for the human rep handling this conversation — whatever you already use (a staff id, an email, a helpdesk agent id). Conversations and the commitments made in them are attributed to it.

Ignored unless this agent has **Attribute work to named agents** enabled in Agent Settings. Until then nothing is stored against it, because this is performance data about identifiable people.

speakerName.description: Optional display name for that rep. Only overwrites a stored name when supplied, so a later call that omits it does not blank a name already recorded.

conversationId.description: The conversation session ID (reused across calls for the same customer while session is active)

customerId.description: The resolved or newly created customer ID

status.description: 'new' if a new conversation was started, 'active' if appended to an existing session

isNewConversation.description: true when this call started a new conversation session

isNewCustomer.description: true when the customer was created by this call

422.description: Validation error — no message/messages, no identity field, or both `endConversation` and `escalate` set on the same request.

503.description: Capture queue unavailable; retry with the same idempotency key

get.description: Returns queued, processing, completed, or terminally failed state. Completed jobs include their extraction result.

error.description: Stable public error present only for terminal failures

404.description: Capture not found in this organization and agent scope

get.summary: Lookup customer by identifier with optional semantic memory
get.description:
Find a customer by internal UUID, phone number, email address, or external ID. At least one identity parameter must be provided.

**topic** — When provided, returns semantically relevant memories ranked by vector similarity instead of the 10 most recent. Also returns a pre-formatted `context` string ready to inject into an LLM prompt and a `tokenCount` estimate.

**autoCreate** — When `true`, automatically creates a new customer record if the identifier is not found. The response will include `isNewCustomer: true`. Use `userName` to set the display name for newly created customers.

This is the primary "plug-and-forget" endpoint for bot integrations. A single call resolves identity, creates new customers, and returns relevant memory context — no internal IDs required.

parameters.name: topic
parameters.description:
Topic or customer message to find relevant memories for. When provided, memories are ranked by semantic relevance.
Omit it at the start of a conversation, before the customer has said why they are calling: the response then leads with any unresolved issue, notes whether this is a repeat customer, and ranks memories by confidence and remaining strength rather than recency. Both modes return `context` and `tokenCount`.

parameters.name: maxTokens
parameters.description: Token ceiling for the returned `context` block, for this call only. Omit to use the agent's configured budget, falling back to the default of 800. Values outside the range are clamped. The response always reports the actual size in `tokenCount`.

parameters.name: explain
parameters.description:
When `true`, each returned memory carries a `scoreDetails` object reporting every term the ranking composite used: `semantic`, `keyword`, `entity`, `temporal`, `importance`, `liveStrength`, `composite`, the `weights` applied, the `threshold` cleared, the retrieval `path` ("full" | "fast" | "fast-empty") and the `source` ("vector" | "keyword" | "both").

A term reports `null` when it was NOT computed on the path that served this request — never `0`. The fast path computes no semantic score, and rows admitted by keyword augmentation are not scored at all, so `null` and `0` are different claims. Diagnostic only: the ranking and the returned set are identical with or without it.

parameters.name: autoCreate
parameters.description: Auto-create customer if not found. Response includes isNewCustomer flag.

200.description: Lookup result with optional semantic memories

isNewCustomer.description: true when customer was auto-created by this call

category.description: Memory category (e.g. preference, customer_profile, purchase_history, pain_point)

memoryType.description: Type of memory (fact, preference, intent, goal)

relevance.description: Semantic similarity score (0-1) — only present when topic is provided

sourceContext.description: Original conversation snippet the memory was extracted from

occurredAt.description: Source conversation occurrence time; rendered into context metadata but not embedded in memory content

context.description: Pre-formatted context string for LLM injection. Ranked by semantic relevance when a topic is given, otherwise a call-opening brief led by any unresolved issue.

tokenCount.description: Estimated token count of the context string

openIssue.description: The unresolved issue the context block leads with. Present only on a lookup without a topic, and only when one is open.

notes.description: The two most recent internal agent notes on this issue — its own conversation's notes when it has any, else the customer's latest. Present only while the issue is open.

memories.content: Had unresolved billing dispute in February
memories.sourceContext: Customer said: I still haven't received my refund from February

memories.content: Has been a customer for 3 years

value.context:
- Had unresolved billing dispute in February
- Has been a customer for 3 years

get.description:
Synthesizes a customer's full cross-channel journey (chat, email, voice, SMS) into a single briefing for a human agent taking over: a chronological journey timeline, key memories, sentiment trend, open-issue detection, and an AI-written narrative summary.

Identify the customer by internal UUID, phone, email, or external ID — exactly like /customers/lookup. The customer is never auto-created.

**narrative=false** skips the AI-written briefing (fast, structured data only). **fresh=true** bypasses the 10-minute cache.

parameters.name: narrative
parameters.description: When "false", skip the AI narrative (structured data only)

parameters.name: fresh
parameters.description: Bypass the cache and rebuild the briefing

journey.summary: Reported damaged order A-4471; KB article didn't help
Followed up on replacement, no response

example.narrative: Ava first contacted via chat about a damaged espresso machine (order A-4471); the KB article didn't help. She emailed twice with no resolution and is considering canceling her premium plan. She called and was escalated — the open issue is the replacement for order A-4471.

post.summary: Ingest a completed conversation for memory extraction
post.description:
Batch import endpoint — enqueue a completed conversation (full message history including both user and assistant turns) for asynchronous memory extraction. Use this for historical imports, CRM sync, or post-processing third-party transcripts. For real-time capture use POST /api/v1/capture instead.

Message roles: `user` is the customer, `assistant` is your bot, `agent` is a human rep who took the conversation over, `system` is metadata. Memory extraction treats every non-`user` role as "our side" — it only cares which side spoke — but the conversation view distinguishes them.

`speakerId` / `speakerName` attribute the conversation and any commitments made in it to a named human rep. Ignored unless that agent has attribution enabled in Agent Settings.

> This endpoint was previously also reachable at > `POST /customers/{id}/memories/capture`. That alias was removed — it > was the same handler under a second name, and it collided confusingly > with the unrelated real-time `POST /api/v1/capture`.

language.description: Optional BCP-47 source-language hint for this turn
BCP-47 fallback for turns without their own language hint

infer.description: Set false to store each non-system message directly rather than infer memories with an LLM. Safety, embedding, exact dedupe, reconciliation, and speaker scope still apply.

speakerId.description: External identifier for the attributed human rep

speakerName.description: Optional display name for the attributed human rep

messages.content: I prefer morning deliveries before 9 AM.
Got it! I'll note your preference for morning deliveries.

post.summary: Resolve where a customer's handoff should go
post.description:
Answers the live transfer question: given this customer, which human destination should take them? The decision itself was made when their last conversation ended, so this is a single indexed read.

**This endpoint always returns 200.** Voice platforms treat a resolver error as a failed transfer, which strands a caller — so an unknown customer, a missing decision, or an internal failure all degrade to the agent's default destination instead of an error status. Check `source` to see which tier answered.

Use `?format=dograh` to get Dograh's `transfer_context` shape directly.

schema.description: At least one identity field is required.

200.description: The resolved destination, or the default when nothing better applies

reasoning.description: Why this destination was chosen for this customer.

get.summary: Preview where a customer would be routed (dashboard test panel)

200.description: The resolution that a live transfer would receive
